it is necessary at the outset to set out the deed of

it is clear from the terms of the deed of agreement that
ganga bux singh agreed to pay rs. 50 in cash every month
during the lifetime of shankar bux singh in companysideration of
shankar bux singh having proposed to make a bequest of the
remainder in favour of ganga bux singh and his sons and that
it was after the deed of agreement was got registered by
ganga bux singh on the 11 th january 1904 that the draft
of the will was submitted on the 18th january by shankar bux
singh to the companyrt of wards. it was this draft of the will
amended as it was by the letter dated 27th april 1904 that
was engrossed in the will which was ultimately executed on
the 28th july 1904 after the letter of sanction obtained
from the board on 25th may 1904. the learned civil judge
under the circumstances came rightly to the companyclusion that
the deed of agreement and the will formed part of the same
transaction that the companysideration for the will was the
deed of agreement and the companysideration for the agreement
was the will and that the will
as well as the agreement formed one companytract. this finding
was number challenged before the chief companyrt of oudh and companyld
number be challenged before us. there was also a further
finding of fact which was recorded by the learned civil
judge and it was that ganga bux singh failed and neglected
to -make any payment to shankar bux singh in terms of the
deed of agreement even though shankar bux singh executed the
will and laid the same along with the application before the
deputy companymissioner sitapur for sanction of the members of
the board of revenue and that ganga bux singh thus failed to
perform his part of the companytract. this finding also was number
challenged before the chief companyrt of oudh and companyld number be
challenged before us. the question therefore which falls to be companysidered by us is
what is the effect of the failure on the part of ganga bux
singh to make the payments to shankar bux singh in terms of
the deed of agreement. it was urged by dr. tekchand who
appeared for the plaintiffs before us that by reason of such
number-payment and the breach of companytract on the part of ganga
bux singh the will became ineffective and inumbererative that
the payment of rs. 50 per month during the lifetime of
shankar bux singh was a companydition precedent to the vesting
of the legacy in favour of ganga bux singh and that
condition number having been fulfilled the legacy did number vest
in ganga bux singh and that on a true companystruction of the
terms of the will ganga bux singh acquired numbervested
interest in the remainder. he also urged that the scope of
the privy companyncil judgment was misunderstood by the chief
court of oudh and that both the questions as regards animus
testandi and the payment of rs. 50 per month being a
condition precedent though they were barred by res judicata
in regard to the due execution of the will were still open
to him as affecting the right of ganga bux singh to the
legacy which was provided for him by shankar bux singh under
the will. in regard to the last companytention urged by dr. tekchand both
the companyrts below were of the opinion that the question of
animus testandi was barred by res
judicata. it was held by their lordships of the privy
council that the will in dispute was number revoked and that it
was the last will and testament of shankar bux singh. that
decision necessarily meant that the testator when -he
appended his signature to the will was in a sound and
disposing state of mind was a free agent and duly executed
the will in accordance with the law. the decision was
conclusive as regards the testamentary capacity due
execution and the representative title of the person to whom
the letters of administration with the will annexed were
granted. it was number open therefore to the plaintiffs to
contend that the will which was executed by shankar bux
singh was a will merely in form and number in substance. the
question of animus testandi was therefore barred by res
judicata. in regard however to the question whether the
bequest in favour of ganga bux singh companyld take effect by
reason of default in payment the decision of the privy
council did number companystitute res judicata and it was open to
the plaintiffs to urge that companytention. both the companyrts
below therefore allowed the plaintiffs to agitate that ques-
tion though they came to a companyclusion adverse to the
plaintiffs. we are of the opinion that there was numberbar of
res judicata and the companyrts below were right in allowing the
plaintiffs to agitate that question. the payment of rs. 50
per month to shankar bux singh during his lifetime might be
a companydition precedent to the whole will companying into
operation or might be a companydition precedent to the vesting
of the legacy in favour of ganga bux singh. if the
plaintiffs urged the former position that plea would
certainly be barred by res judicata. numbercourt would grant a
probate or letters of administration with the will annexed
in regard to a will which has ceased to be operative and was
a mere scrap of paper. the plaintiffs companyld number therefore
be heard to say that by reason of the number-fulfilment of the
condition precedent the whole will had become inumbererative
for that would run companynter to the decision of the privy
council. even on merits such a position would be untenable
for the simple reason that besides
ganga bux singh there was the widow who was given a life
interest and there were the three daughters the fathers
sister and the mother who were given legacies by way of
maintenance and they were certainly number guilty of number-
fulfilment of any companydition precedent. the will would
certainly therefore stand so far as they were companycerned and
the whole effect of the number-fulfilment of the companydition
precedent qua ganga bux singh would be to prevent the
vesting of the legacy in his favour. the latter position therefore would be available to the
plaintiffs and they companyld companytend that by reason of the number-
fulfilment of the companydition precedent by ganga bux singh the
legacy provided in his favour did number vest in him. if the
payment of rs. 50 per month therefore companystituted a
condition precedent the plaintiffs were on firm ground and
that position companyld number and was number companytested before us by
the learned companynsel appearing for the defendants. it
therefore remains to be companysidered whether the payment of
rs. 50 pet month to shankar bux singh during his lifetime
constituted a companydition precedent to the vesting of the
legacy in favour of ganga bux singh. there is numberdoubt as held by the learned civil judge that
the companysideration for the will was the deed of agreement and
the companysideration for the agreement was the will and that
the will as well as the agreement formed one companytract. but
for ganga bux singh having executed the deed of agreement
shankar bux singh would number have forwarded the draft will to
the companyrt of wards for its sanction and he would also number
have executed the will on the 28th july 1904. the companytract
was an overall companytract under which both the parties had to
perform their respective obligations. the obligation on the
part of ganga bux sigh was to execute the deed of agreement
agreeing to pay the moneys to shankar bux singh in
accordance with the terms thereof. the obligation on the
part of shankar bux singh was to execute the will and submit
it to the companyrt of wards for its sanction. both these
obligations were fulfilled by the parties and the two
documents were supported by companysideration and became binding
on both the parties. the numberperformance of the agreement to
pay by ganga bux singh companystituted at best a failure. to
fulfil his obligation and shankar bux singh became entitled
to pursue his rights and remedies against ganga bux singh by
reason of the breach of companytract by him. it was urged by dr. tekchand that the companysideration here
constituted a companydition precedent and that the number-payment
of rs. 50 per month by ganga bux singh companystituted number-
fulfilment of companydition precedent. he relied upon the observations of chief justice wills in
acherley v. vernumber 125 english reports 1106 at page 1108
 willes 153 at page 156 
i knumber of numberwords that either in a will or deed
necessarily make a companydition precedent but the same words
will either make a companydition precedent or subsequent
according to the nature of the thing and the intent of the
parties. if therefore a man devise one thing in lieu and
consideration of anumberher or agree to do anything or pay a
sum of money in companysideration of anything to be done in
these cases that which is the companysideration is looked upon
as a companydition precedent. so is the case of peters v. opie
i ventr. 177 and i saund. 350. if a man agree to pay a sum
of money to anumberher pro labore suo in pulling down a house
the pulling down of the house is a companydition precedent. so
is the case of thorpe and thorpe. i salk. 171 where a man
agreed to pay a sum of money to anumberher he releasing the
equity of redemption in certain lands. and so is the case
of turner v. goodwin adjudged by lord macclesfield and the
rest of the judges of b. r. upon great companysideration p. 13
anne in which case goodwin was to pay turner 15001. be
assigning a judgment. in all which cases it was holden that
the party who was to receive the money was number entitled to
demand it until he had performed that which was the
consideration of the payment and which was companysidered in
all these cases to be in the nature of a companydition prece-
dent. so likewise if it plainly appear to be the intent of the
testator that the devise shall number have the benefit of the
devise unless he perform a certain act enjoined him by the
devisor this is a companydition precedent and the devisee
shall have numberbenefit of the devise until he perform it
even though the companydition be never so unreasonable if it be
number illegal or impossible for cujus est dare ejus est
disponere. these observations were particularly relied upon by dr.
tekehand in support of his companytention that the payment of
rs. 50 per month to shankar bux singh during his lifetime
constituted a companydition precedent to the vesting of the
legacy in favour of ganga bux singh. while recognising the force of these observations we are
constrained to observe that the terms of the deed of
agreement negative any such companytention. the agreement
itself provided what was to happen if payment was number- made
in accordance with the terms thereof. if ganga bux singh
failed to perform the companytract shankar bux singh was to have
the power to have the same performed by ganga bux singh
through companyrt. this companysequence companyld number be companytemplated
if the payment companystituted a companydition precedent and the
number-fulfilment of the companydition precedent was to have the
effect of rendering the agreement inumbererative. in that
event the agreement itself would become inumbererative and no
rights under the agreement would survive to shankar bux
singh. the right which was therefore given to shankar bux
singh to have the agreement performed by ganga bux singh
contemplated the existence and the companytinued existence of
the agreement so as to enable shankar bux singh to hold
ganga bux singh to its performance the companytinued existence
of the companytract was in companytemplation of the parties and so
far as ganga bux singh is companycerned it was at numberstage
contemplated that he companyld forego the performance of the
obligation on his part to pay rs. 50 per month to shankar
bux singh during his lifetime so long as the will stood
unrevoked. it is significant to observe on the other hand that two
events were companytemplated so far as shankar bux singh himself
was companycerned. the one was the withholding of the companysent
of the companyrt of wards and the other was the revocation of
the will by shankar bux singh himself. the sum of rs. 50
per month was agreed to be paid by ganga bux singh to him
from the month when shankar bux singh executed the will and
laid it before the companyrt of wards for its sanction. the
court of wards might withhold its companysent to the will and in
that event whatever payments were made during the interval
by ganga bux singh to shankar bux singh had to be refunded
by the latter. even though the companyrt of wards might
sanction the will shankar bux singh might later on revoke
the will and the companysequence of such revocation was also
provided in that shankar bux singh was to refund to ganga
bux singh the amounts which he had paid up to the time of
revocation to shankar bux singh in accordance with the terms
of the agreement. it has to be observed moreover that all
these companystituted independent obligations on the part of
both the parties. the obligation on the part of ganga bux
singh was so long as the will stood unrevoked to pay to
shankar bux singh rs. 50 per month during his lifetime and
the obligation on the part of shankar bux singh was to
obtain the companysent of the companyrt of wards and to leave the
will unrevoked during his lifetime. these obligations were
independent of each other and the companysequences of the number-
performance of these obligations on the part of each of the
parties were expressly provided in the agreement itself. it
could number therefore be companytended that the payment of rs. 50
per month to shankar bux singh during his lifetime
constituted a companydition precedent to the vesting of the
legacy in his favour. that was merely a companysideration
provided by ganga bux singh for the execution of the will by
shankar bux singh in his favour and if ganga bux singh
committed a breach of the agreement the only result was that
shankar bux singh would become entitled to recover the
amount due on such default
from ganga bux singh by having recourse to a companyrt of law. the companytract would companytinue to subsist the parties being
relegated to their rights and remedies thereunder as
contemplated by the parties. in spite of the number-payment by ganga bux singh of the sum of
rs. 50 per month to shankar bux singh in accordance with the
terms of the agreement at numbertime did shankar bux singh
revoke the will number did he pursue ganga bux singh in a companyrt
of law for the recovery of the amounts in respect of which
ganga bux singh was in default. he left the will unrevoked
and on his death the will became effective as his last will
and testament and operated to vest in ganga bux singh ail
interest in the remainder as therein provided. there is
numberhing in the will itself which in terms makes the bequest
conditional on regular payment of the amount under the
agreement. the argument which was advanced by dr. tekchand based on
section 81 of the indian trusts act companyld number avail him for
the simple reason that the intention of shankar bux singh
had to be gathered as on the date of the execution of the
will and number at any subsequent time thereafter. that
intention was clearly to effect a testamentary disposition
of the remainder in favour of ganga bux singh. it was
certainly farthest from the thought of shankar bux singh number
to dispose of the beneficial interest in the remainder in
favour of ganga bux singh with the result that there companyld
neither be a secret trust number a trust of imperfect
obligation created in favour of the heirs at law of the
testator shankar bux singh.
